Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are already out in the middle now. Rohit Sharma and Yashasvi Jaiswal are the two openers for India. England going with spin straightaway as Joe Root will start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... FOURTH INNINGS ...

England will be really disappointed with their batting performance as even though the wicket is turning and keeping low, it is not one where you get bowled out for 145 runs. They were in an excellent position before the start of Day 3, but have let the hosts take control of this game. They just could not build any significant partnerships and kept losing wickets at regular intervals. Zak Crawley played a fine knock of 60 runs and was the top-scorer while Jonny Bairstow's contributions and a few starts from other batters have helped them post a target of 192 runs. It will be difficult for the bowlers but they will be looking to get a couple of wickets before Stumps to make things interesting here. Join us in a bit for the run chase.

What a turnaround from India! A fantastic effort with the ball led by a stunning five-wicket haul from Ravichandran Ashwin has put the hosts in a firm position to win this Test now. He was well-supported by Kuldeep Yadav who exploited the conditions brilliantly and bagged a fout-fer as well. Ravindra Jadeja chipped in with one as well which meant that all ten wickets were taken by the spinners. Now, the openers will have to see out a tricky few overs in the chase and they will hope to go into Day 4 without losing any wickets.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! That is the end of England as Ravichandran Ashwin gets yet another Five five-wicket haul! James Anderson looking to play the reverse sweep to a flighted ball outside the off stump line and misses it with the bat. The ball hits him on the back leg, lobs on to hit his gloves and falls to the right of Dhruv Jurel who takes a brilliant one-handed catch to send James Anderson back. England are all out for 145 runs.

SESSION SUMMARY - 120 runs and 5 wickets in 33 overs! England embarked on their second innings with a slim lead of 46 runs, but Rohit Sharma's aggressive captaincy led India's resurgence. Deploying close-in fields and starting with spinners, India struck early with Ravichandran Ashwin removing Ben Duckett and Ollie Pope in quick succession. Zak Crawley, however, launched a spirited counterattack, finding the boundary with ease. Partnering with Joe Root, he stabilized England's innings until Ashwin's brilliance claimed his wicket. Jonny Bairstow then joined Crawley, guiding England's lead past the 100-run mark with a crucial partnership. Kuldeep Yadav intervened with a peach to dismiss Crawley. Ben Stokes, surviving a couple of close calls, eventually fell to Kuldeep, leaving Bairstow to hold the fort alongside Ben Foakes. As the match hangs in the balance, both teams will vie for supremacy in the final session. Tune in at 2:30 pm IST (9 am GMT) to witness the thrilling climax.
